title: Noah and the Big Boat
imageAlt: Paper-cut illustration of Noah's ark with animals and a rainbow
bigIdea: God always does what He says He will do.
tellIt: God asked Noah to build a giant boat, even though it had never rained before. Noah obeyed — hammer, hammer, hammer — for a very long time.
Two by two the animals walked in: stompy elephants, hoppy rabbits, slithery snakes. Then God shut the door and the rain came down.
When the water dried up, God painted a rainbow in the sky and promised: I will never flood the whole earth again.
askThem: What is something hard that God might ask you to do?
What do you think of when you see a rainbow?
Who is someone you can trust to keep a promise?

memoryVerse.text: God is not a man, that he should lie... Has he said, and will he not do it?
motions: "God is not a man" — point up, then shake head
"and will he not do it?" — big thumbs up

games.title: Animal Parade Two-by-Two
steps: Give every child one animal card and keep it secret.
On go, everyone makes their animal's sound and finds their match.
Matched pairs march onto the 'ark' (a taped rectangle on the floor).

games.title: Rainbow Freeze
games.supplies: Colored scarves or paper strips, music
steps: Kids dance with a colored scarf while music plays.
When the music stops, call a color — those kids shout the promise: 'God keeps His promises!'
Play until every color has been called.

objectLesson.title: The Promise Jar
objectLesson.supplies: Clear jar, water, a few drops of oil, food coloring
steps: Fill the jar with water — this is the flood.
Add drops of colored oil and stir hard; the color always rises back to the top.
Say: no matter how much you shake it, the oil comes back up — that's how sure God's promises are.

coloringPage.alt: Coloring page line art of Noah's ark with animals and a rainbow
coloringPage.caption: Ark & rainbow — add a color for each promise you can name.

prayer: Thank You, God, that You always keep Your promises. Help us to trust and obey like Noah. Amen.

title: David and Goliath
imageAlt: Paper-cut illustration of young David facing the giant Goliath
bigIdea: You don't have to be big — God is big for you.
tellIt: A giant named Goliath shouted at God's people every single day, and every single day the soldiers were afraid.
David was just a shepherd boy delivering bread and cheese. But he said, 'The Lord who saved me from the lion will save me from this giant.'
One smooth stone, one swing of the sling — and the giant fell. David wasn't strong; God was.
askThem: What feels like a giant to you right now?
What can you say to yourself when you are scared?

memoryVerse.text: The Lord is my strength and my shield; my heart trusts in him.
motions: "The Lord is my strength" — flex both arms
"and my shield" — arms crossed in front

games.title: Five Smooth Stones Toss
games.supplies: 5 crumpled paper balls, a bucket, giant cutout
steps: Stand a cardboard 'giant' with a hole cut where the forehead is.
Each child gets five paper stones and three steps back for each hit.
After each throw, the group shouts the memory verse together.

games.title: Giant Says
steps: Play Simon Says, but the leader is the giant using a big scary voice.
Kids only obey commands that begin with 'God says'.
Point out: we listen to God's voice, not the giant's.

objectLesson.title: The Unliftable Backpack
objectLesson.supplies: A backpack, heavy books, a strong helper
steps: Load a backpack with books until a child can't lift it alone.
Invite a grown-up to lift it while the child keeps a hand on the strap.
Say: the problem didn't shrink — someone stronger carried it. That's God with us.

coloringPage.alt: Coloring page line art of David with a sling facing Goliath
coloringPage.caption: David & Goliath — write your 'giant' on the biggest stone.

prayer: God, You are stronger than anything that scares us. Make our hearts brave today. Amen.

title: Daniel in the Lions' Den
imageAlt: Paper-cut illustration of Daniel praying among calm lions
bigIdea: God is with us even in scary places.
tellIt: Daniel prayed three times a day — morning, noon and night — with his window wide open.
A new law said, 'Pray only to the king!' Daniel opened his window and prayed to God anyway.
They threw him to the lions, but God shut the lions' mouths. In the morning Daniel called out, 'I'm still here!'
askThem: When is a good time for you to pray each day?
Have you ever done the right thing when it was hard?
What do you think Daniel prayed about in the den?

memoryVerse.text: Do not be afraid, for the Lord your God will be with you wherever you go.
motions: "Do not be afraid" — hands on cheeks, then wave 'no'

games.title: Sleeping Lions
steps: Half the class are lions lying down with 'shut mouths'; the rest are Daniels tiptoeing past.
Lions may roar only when the leader rings a bell — but no touching.
Swap roles and talk about how it felt to walk past the lions.

games.title: Three Times a Day Relay
games.supplies: Sun, cloud and moon cards; two baskets
steps: Scatter time-of-day cards across the room.
Teams race to collect one sun, one cloud and one moon.
Each returning runner kneels and says one short prayer word: thanks, sorry, please.

objectLesson.title: The Flashlight in the Box
steps: Let a child look into a dark closed box — scary and empty.
Drop in a lit flashlight and close it again, then look through the peephole.
Say: the box didn't change, but the light did. God's presence is our light in dark places.

coloringPage.alt: Coloring page line art of Daniel praying with lions
coloringPage.caption: Daniel & the lions — draw a window with the sun, clouds and moon.

prayer: Lord, help us pray to You every day, even when it is hard. Thank You for staying close. Amen.

title: Five Loaves and Two Fish
imageAlt: Paper-cut illustration of Jesus feeding a crowd with loaves and fish
bigIdea: Give Jesus your little, and He does a lot.
tellIt: Thousands of people sat on a grassy hill listening to Jesus, and their tummies started to rumble.
One boy had five little loaves and two small fish. He gave it all away to Jesus.
Jesus said thank You to God, broke the bread — and it kept coming and coming. Everyone ate, and twelve baskets were left over!
askThem: What is something small you could share this week?
How do you think the boy felt handing over his lunch?
What do we say to God before we eat?

memoryVerse.text: Give, and it will be given to you.
motions: "and it will be given" — hands scoop back in
"to you" — point to a friend, then yourself

games.title: Basket Pass
games.supplies: Basket, soft bread and fish props, music
steps: Pass the basket around the circle while music plays.
When it stops, that child names one thing they can share.
Keep going until the basket has visited everyone.

games.title: Twelve Baskets Scramble
games.supplies: 12 paper baskets, paper loaves and fish
steps: Hide paper loaves and fish around the room.
Teams gather them into twelve baskets — no basket may be left empty.
Count together to twelve and cheer.

objectLesson.title: One Candle, Many Candles
objectLesson.supplies: Battery tea lights (one lit, many unlit)
steps: Hold up one small light in a dim room.
Use it to 'pass' light to every child's tea light one by one.
Say: the first light never got smaller — that's what happens when we share what we have.

coloringPage.alt: Coloring page line art of a boy holding a basket of loaves and fish
coloringPage.caption: Loaves & fish — draw what you will share this week in the basket.

prayer: Jesus, here is our little. Please use it to bless a lot of people. Amen.

title: The Good Samaritan
imageAlt: Paper-cut illustration of the Good Samaritan with a donkey on a road
bigIdea: A neighbor is anyone who needs kindness.
tellIt: A man walking a lonely road was hurt by robbers and left beside the path.
Two important people saw him — and walked right past on the other side.
Then a Samaritan, someone people said didn't belong, stopped. He bandaged the man, put him on his donkey and paid for his care.
askThem: Who is someone at school that people walk past?
What is one kind thing you can do today?
Why do you think the first two didn't stop?

motions: "your neighbor" — point all around the room

games.title: Bandage Relay
games.supplies: Rolls of crepe paper or gauze
steps: In pairs, one child gently wraps their partner's arm with crepe paper.
Race to the 'inn' (a chair) and back, then swap roles.
Talk about how helping takes time and care, not just words.

games.title: Walk On By / Stop and Help
steps: Read a card: 'Someone drops their books', 'A new kid sits alone'.
Kids run to the STOP side or the WALK ON side of the room.
Ask a volunteer to act out what stopping would look like.

objectLesson.title: The Heavy Bag Nobody Carried
objectLesson.supplies: A grocery bag full of items (make it spill)
steps: Walk in carrying an overloaded bag and let it spill on the floor.
Wait quietly and see who helps; thank the helpers warmly.
Say: noticing is the first half of loving your neighbor.

coloringPage.alt: Coloring page line art of the Good Samaritan helping a traveler
coloringPage.caption: The Good Samaritan — draw yourself somewhere on the road helping.

prayer: Jesus, give us eyes that notice and hands that help. Amen.

title: The Lost Sheep
imageAlt: Paper-cut illustration of a shepherd and his flock at sunset
bigIdea: God comes looking for you — every time.
tellIt: A shepherd counted his sheep at sunset: ninety-seven, ninety-eight, ninety-nine... one was missing!
He left the ninety-nine safe and searched the rocks and thorny bushes until he heard a small 'baa'.
He lifted that sheep onto his shoulders, carried it home and threw a party. That's how heaven feels about you.
askThem: Have you ever been lost? How did it feel to be found?
How does the shepherd feel about the one sheep?
Who can we help feel welcome here?

memoryVerse.text: I am the good shepherd. I know my sheep.
motions: "I am the good shepherd" — hold an invisible staff
"my sheep" — fluffy hands beside your ears

games.title: Baa Baa Blindfold
steps: One blindfolded 'shepherd' stands in the middle of the circle.
A hidden child baas once; the shepherd points toward the sound.
Everyone cheers when the lost sheep is found.

games.title: Count the Flock
steps: Kids count cotton-ball sheep into a pen in groups of ten.
Discover one is missing and search the room together.
Celebrate loudly when it's found — party sound effects encouraged.

objectLesson.title: The Missing Puzzle Piece
objectLesson.supplies: A small puzzle with one piece hidden in your pocket
steps: Build the puzzle together and notice the hole in the middle.
Ask: does the picture still feel finished?
Produce the last piece and say: that's why the shepherd went looking. Everyone matters.

coloringPage.alt: Coloring page line art of a shepherd carrying a lamb
coloringPage.caption: The Lost Sheep — hide one extra sheep in the picture for a friend to find.

prayer: Good Shepherd, thank You for knowing our names and coming to find us. Amen.
